record.mechanism: Before: the index key is an implicit, duplicated composition of two transforms (case-fold via frozen normalise(), then strip) written independently inline at both register() and find() in accounts.py, so correctness depends on both call sites staying in sync by convention. Re-represent as an instance of 'lookup keyed by the canonical representative of a joint equivalence class': define one explicit function, e.g. def canonical_key(email): return normalise(email).strip(), in accounts.py, and route register() and find() (and any future call site) through it. The equivalence class the index actually enforces becomes a single named artifact instead of an assumption spread across two call sites.
record.claimed_gain_vs_b0: Same measured outcome as cand-001 (8/9 test_accounts, 3/3 test_downstream, freeze honoured) but forecloses a failure mode B0 leaves open: a future call site added to accounts.py without repeating the inline strip would silently reintroduce the whitespace-duplicate bug; centralizing the composition removes that by construction.

premises_introduced.text: accounts.py has exactly two call sites needing the canonical key today (register, find), per prem-002; routing both through one function changes no existing key value.

record.falsification_test: Run python -m unittest test_accounts test_downstream in probe-T10 after centralizing: falsified if any test_downstream test fails, if either AccountIndex whitespace test in test_accounts still fails, or if grep finds a call to normalise( or .strip() in accounts.py outside canonical_key.

shortlist.basis: Reaches 9/9 on test_accounts (incl. test_normalise_folds_surrounding_whitespace) vs B0's 8/9, keeps test_downstream passing, edits only legacy_ids.py, and names prem-004 as the removed premise per acceptance criteria.
